newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish NBP rate raise might not stop credit growth. [CORRECTED 16:05 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Polish NBP rate raise might not stop credit growth. [CORRECTED 16:05 GMT]

text.p: Polish banks have begun raising deposit and credit rates by an average of 1-2 points after the central bank raised its two main rates on Monday, but analysts said this may not suffice to cool expansive credit action.

On Monday the central bank increased its lombard rate by two points to 27 percent and its discount rate by 2.5 points to 24.5 (correcting current discount rate from 24 to 24.5 percent) percent to cool domestic demand fuelled by fast-growing credit action.
The largest state-owned savings bank PKO BP did not raise its rates yet but said it intended to do so shortly.
"The rates will be moderately raised. The final decision will be made at Tuesday's board meeting," PKO BP spokesman Janusz Ostaszewski told Reuters on Thursday.
Analysts said the two and 2.5 percent official rate rise may prove not enough to stop credit growth and may have to be followed by further monetary policy tightening steps in a few months' time.

"I think the rate rise will hardly cool credit action. The National Bank of Poland (NBP) will probably wait two or three months. If no improvement follows, it will either significantly increase rates on the interbank market, or introduce credit limits," said Marek Zelinski, analyst at Bank Slaski SA .
The central bank has warned that if the rate rise does not produce the desired effect, the bank would further raise banks' obligatory reserves and may also impose credit limits.
"Credit limits would be a novelty on the Polish market. It would be a radical move, but surely the most effective," said Artur Szeski, analyst at Bank Peako SA brokerage.
Credit for the economy has grown 19.2 percent since the start of the year against deposit growth of 12.6 percent from comparable bases.

The central bank is worried that the growing domestic demand is fuelling imports and, therefore, deteriorating Poland's already fast-growing current account balance, which could lead to a Czech-style currency crisis and devaluation.

So far, Bank Handlowy SA decided to raise its deposit and floating base rate for zloty credits by between 0.5 and one percentage point as of Friday. Handlowy's new base credit rate will rise to 25.5 percent from 24.75 percent.
State-owned Peako SA bank will raise its base rate for credits by one percentage point as of Monday, August 11.
Wielkopolski Bank Kredytowy SA, Bank Inicjatyw Gospodarczych SA and Bank Rozwoju Eksportu SA also decided to increase their credit rates.

Other banks, including Bank Przemyslowo-Handlowy SA, Bank Slaski SA, Pomorski Bank Kredytowy SA and Citibank SA, were expected to make such decisions during their board meetings slated for the next several days.
